Passage: The Molten Sea: Two Thousand or Three Thousand Baths?
Difficulty: The molten sea in the temple is said to contain two thousand baths in 1 Kings 7:26 but to receive and hold three thousand baths in 2 Chronicles 4:5. Readers ask whether the same vessel can have two capacities.
Explanations: Two explanations are offered, and both are compatible with a reliable text. One is a copyist numeral variant of the same kind as the stalls (two thousand for three thousand). The other is a difference in measure: two thousand baths as its ordinary working capacity, three thousand when filled to the brim. Either explanation leaves the vessel's description — a handbreadth thick, lily-work brim, standing on twelve oxen — identical, and no claim of the passage turns on the bath figure.
SiteAssessment: Site assessment: The difference is most simply a numeral or measure variant in transmission. It does not affect what the molten sea was, where it stood, or what it signified.
